issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may interfere under Article 136 with concurrent factual findings in a criminal matter when the High Court has acted perversely or otherwise improperly.
material_facts: The appeals arose from convictions affirmed by the High Court as to the appellants’ participation, although the High Court reduced the principal offence and altered the related conviction.
The appellants argued that both courts had overlooked material evidence and serious infirmities in the prosecution case.
The Supreme Court found that the courts below had summarily dealt with the evidence and had overlooked manifest errors and glaring infirmities.
issues.conclusion: Article 136 permits interference with factual findings, including concurrent findings, where the High Court acted perversely or otherwise improperly; the Court found that threshold met in this case.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 136, the Supreme Court ordinarily does not disturb concurrent findings of fact in criminal matters, but may do so in exceptional circumstances, including where the High Court has acted perversely or otherwise improperly. The Court relied on The State of Madras v. A. Vaidyanatha Iyer, Himachal Pradesh Administration v. Shri Om Prakash, Balak Ram v. State of U.P., Arunachalam v. P.S.R. Sadhananthan, State of U.P. v. Hamit Singh, and State of U.P. v. Pheru Singh.

predicates.criminal_special_leave_appeal: The matter is a criminal appeal brought before the Supreme Court by special leave.
predicates.concurrent_factual_findings: The courts below reached concurrent findings of fact relevant to the appeal.
predicates.high_court_acted_perversely_or_improperl: The High Court reached its findings through perverse or otherwise improper treatment of the case.

issues.definition: When a criminal special-leave appeal challenges concurrent factual findings and the High Court acted perversely or improperly, the Supreme Court may interfere with those findings.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction cannot safely stand when the prosecution evidence is unreliable and the courts below have overlooked material infirmities in assessing it.
material_facts: The earliest written report did not specify the place of occurrence, and the police record and witness evidence gave inconsistent indications about its location.
The report was lodged several hours after the occurrence, despite the witnesses being at a hospital close to the police station; the Court rejected the explanation for the delay.

The medical officer had sent an earlier intimation to the police, but the investigating officer denied knowing about it and gave an account of his actions that conflicted with other witnesses’ evidence.

The witnesses had a history of hostility and criminal cases involving the opposing side; their accounts were inconsistent, one witness did not implicate all the accused, and the evidence of the injured witness was also found unreliable.
The lower courts accepted the prosecution witnesses’ accounts without adequately addressing the significant inconsistencies and infirmities.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution evidence fell short of reliability and acceptability, making it unsafe to act upon; the charges were not established by cogent, reliable, and trustworthy evidence. The Court set aside the convictions and sentences and acquitted the appellants.
issues.legal_principle: A conviction must rest on cogent, reliable, and trustworthy evidence; evidence that falls short of reliability and acceptability is unsafe to act upon. In this criminal appeal under Article 136, the Court could set aside the convictions where the lower courts’ assessment overlooked manifest errors and glaring infirmities.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.prosecution_evidence_unreliable: The prosecution evidence contains serious credibility problems, including material inconsistencies, unexplained delay, or unreliable witness testimony.
predicates.material_infirmities_overlooked: The courts below failed to address material errors or glaring weaknesses in the evidence.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal challenges a conviction, the prosecution evidence is unreliable, and the courts below overlooked material infirmities, the conviction is set aside and the accused is acquitted.
